$comment: DOCS-AUDIT-3. Binds every published number that traces to a benchmark run to the artifact it
came from, so a future measurement change makes the published page FAIL a check instead of
silently diverging from it. This is the machine-readable half of docs/published-claims-inventory.md
(DOCS-AUDIT-1); that file stays the human narrative, this one is what CI can run.
Deliberately a CHECKER, not a generator: both published artifacts are hand-authored HTML with no
build step (see the two-artifacts rule), and regenerating them would replace prose written by a
person with template output. Making divergence loud achieves the chunk's goal without that.
Claims with NO artifact - external/competitor figures cited from papers, and narrative about
past runs - are listed in `untraceable` so their absence here is a recorded decision rather
metric: a key of a systems[] entry in the run's longmemeval_s_terransoul.json.
scale/decimals: how the artifact value is rendered before matching (0.9504 -> 95.0 at 1dp).
needle: the EXACT published substring, with {value} where the number appears.

artifacts.$comment-arms: head-full500-* is the canonical set: one embedder (embeddinggemma) AND one code version (HEAD, 2026-07-27), one arm per process. The max100-full500-* arms are 2026-07-25 code, and max100-full500/ additionally ran the harness-default embedder — both kept on disk as evidence, neither safe to compare across.

requireSameEmbedder.$comment: Every artifact compared against another in the same claim must share an embedder. The chat arm was run without LONGMEM_EMBED_MODEL and silently used the harness default (mxbai-embed-large) while the others used embeddinggemma, which invalidated a cross-arm comparison for a full day before anyone read the report headers. This turns that into a failure.

claims.note: The >= makes this strictly false whenever the measured value is below the published one.

Claim 3 of the inventory. Binds to the CHAT arm because the sentence describes chat. The surrounding 'byte-identical' assertion is a prose claim this checker cannot evaluate - it is refuted by any measured difference between chat and rrf.

untraceable.why: Competitor/baseline numbers quoted from cited papers. They must trace to a source citation, not to a run of ours; checking them against our artifacts would be a category error.

untraceable.what: 'use in RAG ... recall-at-ten 68.3 percent' in memory-evolution.html

untraceable.why: Narrative about a past investigation, not a current claim. Records what was believed at the time.
No full-500 artifact exists for it. MAX-100-3 fixed the cross-lingual tokenizer but the JD vi/ja re-measurement is still owed, so there is nothing to bind to yet.
